description: Location and city-tier based adjustments for health insurance recommendations.

metro.description: Large metro cities usually have higher hospitalization, room, and treatment costs.

high_sum_insured.reason: Treatment costs are generally higher in metro cities.
high_sum_insured.customer_friendly_reason: Hospitals in metro cities can be expensive, so a higher cover may be useful.

room_rent_flexibility.reason: Room costs are generally higher in metro hospitals.
room_rent_flexibility.customer_friendly_reason: Room rent flexibility can help reduce restrictions during hospitalization.

tier_1.description: Large non-metro city with moderate-to-high healthcare costs.

high_sum_insured.reason: Treatment costs can still be significant in tier 1 cities.
high_sum_insured.customer_friendly_reason: A reasonably higher cover can help manage treatment costs.

room_rent_flexibility.reason: Room category restrictions can affect claim payout.
room_rent_flexibility.customer_friendly_reason: Some room rent flexibility can be useful during hospitalization.

tier_2.description: Mid-sized city with moderate healthcare costs.

high_sum_insured.reason: Medical inflation still supports adequate cover even outside metro cities.
high_sum_insured.customer_friendly_reason: Adequate cover is still important even if treatment costs are lower than metros.

small_town.description: Smaller town where local treatment costs may be lower, though referral to larger cities may happen.

high_sum_insured.reason: Local treatment costs may be lower, but base cover requirement remains.
high_sum_insured.customer_friendly_reason: Your cover should still be adequate, especially if treatment may happen in a larger city.
